issues.description: Negated compound condition reads awkwardly; a small helper would make intent self-evident
issues.detail: The check `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` correctly distinguishes a statement-form `@layer foo;` from a block-form `@layer foo {}`, but the negated conjunction is harder to scan than the surrounding positive equality checks. A tiny named predicate like `isLayerStatement(node)` (returning `nodeName === 'layer' && node.nodes === undefined`) would let the main expression keep its parallel `nodeName !== X` shape. Data dominates here: the real distinction is statement vs block, and naming it makes the algorithm obvious.

issues.description: `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` is more ceremony than needed
issues.detail: PostCSS containers either have a `nodes` array or they don't; a direct `node.nodes === undefined` (or `!node.nodes`) reads the same and matches the style used elsewhere in the file. The `typeof` guard is defensive against a case that doesn't arise for AtRule nodes from PostCSS. Small thing, but the rule body is dense enough that every extra token costs scan time.

issues.description: Test coverage could add the block-with-children and statement-form-after-import cases
issues.detail: The new test covers `@layer foo {}` (empty block) before `@import`. The fix keys on `node.nodes === undefined`, so a block with actual contents (`@layer foo { .a {} }`) exercises the same path but guards against future refactors that might check emptiness instead of presence. Also worth a passing case for `@layer foo;` (statement form) before `@import` to lock in that the existing layer-exception still holds. Cheap to add; makes the data-shape distinction the code now relies on explicit in the tests.

review.summary: Small, correct, well-scoped fix. The data structure was already telling the truth — a layer with a block has `nodes`, a layer statement does not — and the patch leans on that distinction, which is the right move. My only quibbles are stylistic: the negated compound predicate would read better as a named helper, `typeof ... === 'undefined'` is heavier than the equality check used nearby, and the test set could add a non-empty layer block plus a statement-form layer to pin the shape distinction down. SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE; ship after the cosmetics if you care, ship as-is if you don't.
